problem: Imitation learning methods require large amounts of high-quality demonstrations including expert actions, which are often unavailable.
approach: LWAIL uses Wasserstein distance computed in a dynamics-aware latent space trained via Intention Conditioned Value Function (ICVF) pretraining to enable state-only distribution matching with minimal expert episodes.
contribution: Achieves expert-level performance using only one or a few state-only expert episodes, outperforming prior Wasserstein-based and adversarial IL methods on MuJoCo environments.

problem: AI agents deployed in real-world settings pose significant safety risks, but existing benchmarks rely on simulated environments and narrow task domains that inadequately assess real-world safety.
approach: OpenAgentSafety evaluates agents interacting with real tools (web browsers, code executors, file systems, bash, messaging) across 350+ multi-turn tasks spanning benign and adversarial intents, combining rule-based and LLM-as-judge assessments.
contribution: Reveals that 51.2%-72.7% of safety-vulnerable tasks produce unsafe behavior across five prominent LLMs, highlighting critical risks before deployment.

problem: LLMs trained on single reasoning modalities (typically natural language) miss synergies between complementary representational formats for logical reasoning.
approach: Mixture-of-Thought (MoT) enables LLMs to jointly learn from self-generated rationales across natural language, code, and a new symbolic modality (truth-table) that enumerates logical cases.
contribution: Achieves up to 11.7pp average accuracy gain on FOLIO and ProofWriter benchmarks compared to single-modality chain-of-thought approaches.

problem: Federated learning with heterogeneous model architectures cannot use standard parameter aggregation methods, and data heterogeneity limits generalization on unseen data.
approach: Clients share feature distribution statistics (mean/covariance) with the server, then train variational transposed CNNs using Gaussian latent samples to generate synthetic data for fine-tuning.
contribution: Improves generalization accuracy compared to model-heterogeneous FL frameworks while reducing communication costs and memory consumption.

problem: Video reasoning in LVLMs lacks challenging multi-hop questions and high-quality video-grounded Chain-of-Thought data needed to bootstrap reasoning enhancement via reinforcement learning.
approach: ReWatch-R1 uses a multi-agent ReAct framework to synthesize video-grounded CoT by simulating re-watching and information retrieval, then post-trains with SFT and RLVR using an Observation & Reasoning reward mechanism.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on five challenging video reasoning benchmarks with improved reasoning grounding and reduced hallucination.

problem: 3D scene generation from single images fails to organize part-level objects into distinct instances because internal assignment mechanisms lack structural constraints.
approach: SceneTransporter formulates structured 3D scene generation as a global correlation assignment problem solved via entropic Optimal Transport within the compositional DiT denoising loop, enforcing one-to-one routing and coherent grouping.
contribution: Significantly improves instance-level coherence and geometric fidelity in open-world scene generation compared to existing methods.

problem: Current video benchmarks for multimodal models focus on simple perception tasks that only require matching question-mentioned frames, not multi-frame reasoning or analysis of hidden information.
approach: MMR-V defines long-range multi-frame reasoning tasks requiring inference across far-distant evidence frames and hidden information beyond direct perception, with manually annotated questions and distractor strategies.
contribution: Reveals that even the best-performing model (Gemini-2.5-pro) achieves only 64.3% accuracy and that current reasoning enhancement strategies bring limited gains, indicating a gap in multimodal reasoning capabilities.

problem: First-frame-guided video editing provides limited fine-grained control over the temporal evolution of edits across the entire video.
approach: Uses mask-based LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained Image-to-Video models with spatiotemporal masks to teach preservation of source content or generation of novel content, with optional temporal consistency or reference-guided synthesis.
contribution: Enables users to control the entire temporal evolution of complex edits like object rotation or flower blooming, outperforming baseline methods in video editing performance.

problem: Joint human-scene reconstruction from monocular video produces noisy geometry and artifacts that cause motion-tracking and scene interaction policies to fail.
approach: CRISP fits convex planar primitives to depth-based point clouds via clustering, uses human-scene contact modeling to reconstruct occluded geometry, and ensures physical plausibility through RL-driven humanoid control.
contribution: Reduces motion-tracking failure rates from 55.2% to 6.9% on EMDB and PROX benchmarks while delivering 43% faster RL simulation throughput for robotics applications.

problem: Existing multimodal models operate offline and cannot handle real-time interactive video understanding with sequential questions, memory constraints, and future anticipation.
approach: RIVER Bench introduces Retrospective Memory, Live-Perception, and Proactive Anticipation tasks with real-time interactive format evaluating models on streaming video comprehension, revealing deficiencies in long-term memory and future perception.
contribution: Demonstrates that offline models struggle with real-time processing and proposes a general improvement method enabling flexible real-time user interaction.

problem: Continual vision-language learning must maintain stable yet plastic capability under non-stationary streams without storing raw data, preventing catastrophic forgetting and maintaining transfer.
approach: CoMem organizes knowledge into a compact concept-relation graph, rehearses by conditioning practice signals on sampled subgraphs, and uses compositional consistency objectives and uncertainty-aware filtering.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art retention and transfer with consistent gains on cross-domain retrieval, concept learning, and continual VQA under matched memory and parameter budgets.

problem: Existing RAG systems lack methods for LLMs to proactively ask clarifying questions when faced with underspecified queries, as they ignore rule-based reasoning structures embedded in retrieved knowledge.
approach: GPS uses Directed Acyclic Graph reasoning with theoretical completeness guarantees to capture condition logic in retrieved knowledge, combines traversal-based pruning with user responses, and applies RL with hybrid reward.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines in both answer accuracy and interaction cost through targeted state probing and dynamic DAG-based clarification.

problem: Weight pruning LLMs is challenging because estimating global weight importance across massive parameters is infeasible, and uniform sparsity ratios across layers fail to account for uneven layer contributions.
approach: LSA allocates layer-wise sparsity by quantifying importance through minimal linear reconstruction error (LSE) when removing 50% of least important weights, supporting non-uniform block-level granularity.
contribution: At 70% overall sparsity, LSA surpasses state-of-the-art methods across language modeling and seven zero-shot tasks while supporting flexible per-block pruning.

problem: Vision Transformers process global [CLS] tokens and local patch tokens identically despite their distinct natures, causing friction in learning both global and local features effectively.
approach: Proposes specialized processing paths that disentangle [CLS] and patch token flow through normalization layers and early QKV projections based on analysis showing implicit differentiation between token types.
contribution: Improves segmentation by over 2 mIoU points on standard benchmarks while maintaining classification accuracy with only 8% parameter increase and no computational overhead.

problem: Self-supervised RL feature learning via mutual information skill learning (MISL) lacks theoretical understanding of how representation parametrization enables identifiable recovery of environment features.
approach: Analyzes Contrastive Successor Features (CSF) through identifiable representation learning, proving CSF recovers ground-truth features up to linear transformation due to inner-product parametrization and skill diversity.
contribution: Provides first identifiability guarantee for representation learning in RL, explaining implications of different MI objectives; validated on MuJoCo and DeepMind Control from both states and pixels.

problem: Scaling multimodal models to 3D medical imaging is computationally expensive because existing methods rely on 2D slices or fixed-token compression that disrupts volumetric continuity.
approach: Photon uses instruction-conditioned token scheduling with surrogate gradient propagation to adaptively reduce tokens during training/inference, incorporates custom backpropagation for differentiable discrete optimization, and applies regularization to mitigate bias.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on diverse medical visual question answering tasks while reducing resource usage and accelerating both training and inference.

problem: Existing reward methods for GUI agents struggle to generalize due to lack of ground-truth trajectories and application databases, while static trajectory-based LLM-as-Judge approaches suffer from limited accuracy.
approach: ProRe uses a general-purpose reasoner that schedules targeted state probing tasks executed by domain-specific evaluator agents, collecting additional environment observations to assign more accurate rewards.
contribution: Improves reward accuracy and F1 score by up to 5.3% and 19.4% respectively, with policy agents achieving up to 22.4% success rate improvement over baselines.

problem: GPU kernel writing is highly iterative and challenging, requiring domain expertise to improve performance through execution feedback, making it suitable for RL but lacking multi-turn training recipes.
approach: Kevin applies multi-turn RL with novel recipes for long trajectories and effective reward attribution across turns to train on CUDA kernel generation and optimization using verifiable rewards (correctness and speedup).
contribution: Improves kernel correctness from 56% to 82% and mean speedup from 0.53x to 1.10x of PyTorch Eager baseline, surpassing o4-mini and showing higher improvement rates with more refinement turns.

problem: Long-context models are susceptible to contextual noise from irrelevant tokens that can mislead attention, yet the role of noise in degrading performance is not well understood.
approach: Uses Integrated Gradient scores to detect and quantify noise information within context, proposes Context Denoising Training (CDT) that improves attention on critical tokens while reinforcing their influence on predictions.
contribution: CDT significantly boosts model attention on critical tokens; when trained with CDT, an 8B open-source model achieves performance (50.92) comparable to GPT-4o (51.00) across four tasks.

problem: Training computer-use agents requires massive amounts of manually annotated GUI interaction data, which is prohibitively expensive to acquire at scale.
approach: VideoAgentTrek automatically mines training data from YouTube tutorial videos by developing Video2Action with a video grounding model detecting GUI actions and an action-content recognizer extracting structured parameters.
contribution: From 39,000 YouTube videos generates 1.52 million interaction steps; improves OSWorld-Verified success from 9.3% to 15.8% (70% relative gain) and AgentNetBench step accuracy from 64.1% to 69.3%.

problem: Different rank aggregation methods produce significantly different results, impacting applications like AI agent development and evaluation, but no principled method exists for selecting which aggregation rule to use.
approach: Designs a data-driven rule-picking rule (RPR) that maximizes consistency if the data collection process were repeated, without assuming a generative model, and provides a sampling-based implementation.
contribution: Satisfies consistency-related axioms failed by natural RPRs and provides insights into improving consistency on both statistical models and real-world data.

problem: Standard representational similarity methods produce asymmetric results lacking global alignment scores and struggle with networks of different depths due to restriction to rigid one-to-one layer correspondences.
approach: Hierarchical Optimal Transport (HOT) jointly infers soft, globally consistent layer-to-layer couplings allowing source neurons to distribute mass across multiple target layers, minimizing transport cost under marginal constraints.
contribution: Matches or surpasses standard pairwise matching in alignment quality across vision models, LLMs, and visual cortex recordings while naturally handling depth mismatches through mass distribution.

problem: Representation alignment for generation typically assumes stronger global performance (ImageNet1K accuracy) leads to better generation, but the actual driver of generation performance is unclear.
approach: Conducts large-scale empirical analysis across 27 vision encoders, revealing spatial structure rather than global performance drives generation; proposes iREPA with convolution layer replacement and spatial normalization.
contribution: iREPA consistently improves REPA convergence speed across diverse encoders and model sizes with a 4-line modification, demonstrating spatial information transfer is critical for generation.

problem: Few-shot VQA performance of LMMs using in-context learning does not improve monotonically with more examples because extraneous image information overwhelms the model.
approach: Meta-Adaptive Prompt Distillation uses meta-learning to induce few-shot capabilities through fixed soft prompts distilled from task-relevant features adapted at test time via an attention-mapper module.
contribution: Achieves 21.2% improvement over ICL on VL-ICL Bench and 7.7% further enhancement compared to parameter-efficient finetuning methods for rapid task adaptation.

problem: LLMs typically acquire behaviors from demonstrations or experience, yet much training data consists of symbolic descriptions (instructions, rules, strategies) that specify procedures without examples.
approach: Programming by Backprop (PBB) enables LLMs to execute behaviors directly from abstract symbolic descriptions through targeted finetuning, tested on source code and grammar rules.
contribution: Shows LLMs can internalize reusable procedural abstractions from symbolic descriptions, generalizing across inputs and benefiting from chain-of-thought reasoning, though full reliability remains a challenge.

problem: Existing LiDAR compression methods rely on computationally intensive 3D contexts like voxels and octrees that struggle to balance compression efficiency with coding speed.
approach: Proposes a neural LiDAR compressor using 2D context models with multi-scale spatial, optical-flow temporal, and camera cross-modal context to reduce latency while enabling joint geometry-intensity compression.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements in both rate-distortion performance and coding speed compared to existing methods while supporting universal geometry-intensity compression.

problem: Designing synthesizable 3D ligands for protein pockets is hindered by lack of accurate synthesizability metrics and inconsistencies among classical metrics.
approach: Proposes SYNC, an SE(3)-invariant synthesizability classifier for SBDD and establishes a paradigm using guided diffusion and Direct Preference Optimization to generate synthesizable molecules.
contribution: SYNC demonstrates superior generalizability and speed compared to existing metrics; guided synthesis generates highly synthesizable molecules without compromising binding affinity.

problem: Existing video generation methods depend on fine-tuning large-scale models for specific tasks, which becomes impractical as model sizes grow; fine-grained frame-level control is needed.
approach: Frame Guidance applies training-free guidance to video diffusion models using frame-level signals (keyframes, styles, sketches, depth) via latent processing and optimization strategies for global coherence.
contribution: Produces high-quality controlled videos across diverse tasks including keyframe guidance, stylization, and looping without any training or explicit domain knowledge.

problem: Multimodal models struggle to detect academic fraud in visual evidence from retracted papers because existing benchmarks lack real-world complexity and task diversity.
approach: THEMIS evaluates MLLMs on 4K+ questions spanning 7 scenarios from authentic retracted cases and synthetic data with 16 fine-grained manipulation operations and 5 core fraud reasoning capabilities.
contribution: Even the best-performing model falls below passing threshold, demonstrating THEMIS presents a stringent test for complex, real-world fraud detection tasks.

problem: Predicting complex physical systems is hindered by the lack of expensive real-world data, resulting in models trained primarily on simulations that fail to bridge the sim-to-real gap.
approach: RealPDEBench integrates real-world measurements with paired simulations across five physical systems, defines three tasks comparing real and simulated data, and benchmarks ten representative baselines.
contribution: Reveals significant discrepancies between simulated and real-world data; pretraining with simulated data consistently improves both accuracy and convergence, advancing sim-to-real transfer.

problem: Incomplete multi-view multi-label learning must integrate information under simultaneous view and label incompleteness while maintaining robustness and avoiding over-alignment.
approach: PCVE formulates a principled objective maximizing variational evidence lower bound with permutation-consistent regularization to encourage distributional consistency across views and masked multi-label learning for missing labels.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods in multi-label classification with improved cross-view semantic cohesion and preservation of discriminative capacity.

problem: Current LLMs achieve high single-function verification but fail catastrophically at compositional reasoning across multi-function programs with interacting components.
approach: DafnyCOMP benchmark systematically evaluates LLMs on compositional specification generation for programs composed of 2-5 functions with data dependencies via LLM-driven synthesis.
contribution: Reveals 92% performance gap: while syntax correctness remains >99% for single-function tasks, it drops to 95.67% and verification crashes to 3.69% for compositional tasks.

problem: Set-based gait recognition overlooks short-range temporal context while sequence-based approaches fail to capture long-range temporal dependencies effectively.
approach: GaitSnippet conceptualizes gait as a composition of individualized actions represented by frames randomly selected from continuous segments (snippets), enabling multi-scale temporal context learning.
contribution: Achieves rank-1 accuracy of 77.5% on Gait3D and 81.7% on GREW using 2D CNN backbone, demonstrating effectiveness of snippet-based approach for comprehensive gait feature learning.

problem: Existing long-context LLM benchmarks lack narrative coherence, cover narrow domains, and only test simple recall-oriented tasks, limiting evaluation of true memory abilities.
approach: BEAM benchmark automatically generates up to 10M token coherent conversations with diverse topics and probing questions targeting multiple memory abilities; proposes LIGHT framework with three memory systems.
contribution: BEAM shows 1M-token context models struggle as dialogues lengthen; LIGHT consistently improves performance 3.5%-12.69% across various models by implementing long-term episodic, short-term working, and scratchpad memory.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action models relying on latent actions for VLA pretraining have not fully explored how latent actions can be learned and incorporated for improved generalization.
approach: villa-X advances latent action modeling by improving how latent actions are learned and integrated into VLA pretraining, enabling zero-shot latent action plan generation for unseen embodiments.
contribution: Achieves superior performance across diverse SIMPLER simulation tasks and real-world robotic setups with gripper and dexterous hand manipulation compared to prior VLA approaches.

problem: Scaling diffusion transformers to generate long-context videos is fundamentally limited by quadratic self-attention cost, making memory and computation intractable for long sequences.
approach: Reframes long-context video generation as information retrieval and proposes Mixture of Contexts (MoC), a learnable sparse attention routing module that dynamically selects informative chunks with causal routing.
contribution: Achieves near-linear scaling efficiency by allocating compute to salient history, preserving identities, actions, and scenes over minutes of content without loop closures.

problem: LLM-based global optimization often struggles in high-dimensional search spaces or without domain-specific priors, leading to sparse or uninformative candidate suggestions.
approach: HOLLM partitions the search space into promising subregions selected via bandit-inspired scoring, with LLMs proposing high-quality candidates within each subregion without explicit domain knowledge.
contribution: Consistently matches or surpasses leading global optimization methods while substantially outperforming global LLM-based sampling strategies on standard optimization benchmarks.

problem: Generating synchronized audio-video content is challenging because ensuring precise temporal alignment between audio and visual components while maintaining quality is non-trivial.
approach: JavisDiT uses a Diffusion Transformer for synchronized generation with a Hierarchical Spatial-Temporal Synchronized Prior Estimator extracting fine-grained spatio-temporal priors to guide audio-video alignment.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in both generation quality and synchronization precision on the new JavisBench with 10,140 high-quality text-captioned sounding videos.

problem: Existing multi-person 4D human-scene reconstruction from monocular video requires multi-stage pipelines, iterative refinement, and heavy dependencies (detection, depth estimation, SLAM), limiting real-time performance.
approach: Human3R uses parameter-efficient visual prompt tuning on CUT3R to jointly recover multiple SMPL-X bodies, dense 3D scenes, and camera trajectories in a single forward pass without iterative refinement.
contribution: Achieves superior or competitive performance in global human motion, mesh recovery, video depth, and pose estimation with a single unified model at real-time speed (15 FPS) on 8GB memory.

problem: Traditional mutual information estimators struggle with data that poses difficulties for conventional approaches, particularly in complex domains.
approach: InfoBridge leverages diffusion bridge models to frame mutual information estimation as a domain transfer problem, constructing an unbiased estimator via bridge matching.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on three standard MI estimation benchmarks (low-dimensional, image-based, high MI) and on real-world protein language model embeddings.
